reason: Their only live posting, an IT Manager reporting directly to the COO, asks one hire to keep systems running while also 'migrating our systems to co-location and cloud, as well as modernization of our identity stack' in an environment with 'some inherited technical debt' and partner-driven security obligations - a US console/PC studio of ~45-100 with no technical-operations owner above the IT layer, which is exactly the layer Ben owns.

Headcount reported 68 at acquisition, 74 on its LinkedIn org record, '100+' on its own About page, and ~45 as of Oct 2025 per Grokipedia following Aug 2025 layoffs - figures conflict, treat as roughly 45-100. ~$15M annual revenue (Exa org record, aggregator data).

evidence_jobs.title: IT Manager
evidence_jobs.quote: In addition, you will also be driving meaningful infrastructure projects such as migrating our systems to co-location and cloud, as well as modernization of our identity stack.

people_spec: COO - named in the posting as the role's direct report line and therefore the owner of this problem; the primary buyer

NOTE: do not look for a CTO, VP Engineering, Head of IT or Director of Infrastructure at this company - the posting shows the ops layer reports into the COO with 'existing IT staff' but no named technical-operations leader, which is the signal itself. The Tech Director (if present) is the affected party, not the buyer.
talk_track: I spent five years owning identity and cloud operations for Pokemon's consumer platforms, then built the shared technical-operations org covering four studios at Prytania Media. Your IT Manager posting asks one person to keep systems running and documentation current while also "migrating our systems to co-location and cloud, as well as modernization of our identity stack" - reporting to the COO. Those are two jobs on two different clocks. Support always wins the day, so the migrations quietly slip a quarter or two and nobody can name the week it happened. The part worth having before you hire: identity is what your partner security obligations actually rest on, so it is the piece to sequence first and own separately from the help-desk load. Is the co-lo date already committed to a partner?
